kill.text: Price below $11: near tangible book x1.5; re-test credit and growth
Personal loan net charge-offs above 4% (all-in about 3.4% now)
Member growth below 20% for two quarters (now 35%)

tam.market: US consumer lending, deposits and digital banking, plus financial technology services
tam.source: ValueInvestor estimate: US consumer banking and lending revenue pool for prime and near-prime digital customers ~$400B (personal, student, home loans, deposits, cards).
tam.why_share: SoFi's ~$5B 2026 revenue is ~1.3% of the pool; members growing 35% a year support ~3% by 2031.
tam.what_must_go_right: Charge-offs stay under ~4%; net margin reaches ~22% (like a strong consumer bank); no large dilution beyond ~1.35B shares.

sections.industry_map: SoFi is a national bank and fintech: personal, student and home loans; deposits and checking; investing and crypto; a loan platform business that originates loans for third parties; and Galileo/Technisys technology serving other fintechs and banks.
sections.size_growth: US consumer lending and digital banking are very large markets; SoFi is taking share. Q3 2026 adjusted net revenue $1.37B (+44%), members 17.1M (+35%), deposits $51.3B (SoFi Q3 8-K, Oct 2026). Cyclical with credit and rates.
sections.structure: Competes with large banks (JPMorgan, Capital One), fintechs (Chime, Nubank-like models, Upstart, LendingClub) and brokers. Bank charter gives cheap deposit funding.
sections.demand_supply: Loan demand strong: originations $16.9B (+71%), including $3.8B for third parties. Funding plentiful from deposits. Credit is the swing factor.
sections.industry_risks: (1) Consumer credit downturn - medium/high; warning: charge-offs and delinquencies. (2) Rate path - medium/medium; warning: net interest margin. (3) Regulation (CFPB, capital rules) under a Democrat Congress - medium/medium. (4) Crypto volatility - medium/low (net crypto revenue only $1.6M).
sections.outlook: Near: 2026 guide adjusted revenue ~$5.04B (+40%), net income ~$840M, EPS ~$0.61. Mid: operating leverage and fee businesses lift returns; 2030 goal of 100M products. Long: a top-10 US consumer bank by customers.
sections.winners: Low-cost deposits, cross-sell (products per member 1.56), credit underwriting, brand with young professionals, technology platform.
sections.business: Adjusted EBITDA $470M (34% margin); net income $241M; tangible book value $7.48/share (+25%); CET1 16.9%. Personal loan charge-offs 2.26% reported, ~3.4% including loan sales.
sections.right_to_win: One app that bundles lending, banking and investing for high-income young professionals, funded by a bank charter that most fintechs lack.
sections.moat: Narrow and emerging: charter plus cross-sell scale. Trend: improving.
sections.tam_competitors: Small share of US deposits (~$51B vs ~$2.5T at JPMorgan). Competitors: Capital One, Chime, LendingClub, Upstart, Robinhood.
sections.management: CEO Anthony Noto (since 2018, ex-Twitter CFO, Goldman). Has delivered on guidance; history of dilutive raises. Insider buying small ($0.5M) vs selling $3.2M.
sections.financials: The engine's revenue history is distorted by bank XBRL tags; reported adjusted net revenue rose from ~$2.1B (2023) to ~$5.0B guided for 2026. Profitable since 2024. Share count rising ~24% a year historically (raises and conversions); leverage and 'FCF' flags are normal for a lender funding loan growth.
sections.company_risks: (1) Credit - KPI: personal loan charge-offs. (2) Capital - KPI: CET1. (3) Dilution - KPI: share count. (4) Loan platform dependence - KPI: third-party volume.
sections.variant_view: The market sees SoFi as a richly priced fintech at ~27x earnings; we think the bank is compounding tangible book at 25% and members at 35%, so earnings can grow fast enough to justify a higher value, but credit risk and dilution keep us at a modest position.
sections.valuation: Our value (owner earnings $0.75/share, 22% then 12%, 12% discount): low $12, base $24, high $34; price $16.2 is 33% below base. P/TBV ~2.2x. Street mean $20.8 (23 analysts). Required margin of safety 50% (high-growth, early) gives entry $12. Ming's cost $15.40 (+6%): hold.
sections.pillars: (1) Member growth above 25% - breach below 20%. (2) Charge-offs under 4% - breach above. (3) Tangible book growth above 15% - breach below 10%. (4) No large dilutive raise - breach: equity raise above 5%.
sections.catalysts_flow: Q4 2026 results and 2027 guide (late Jan 2027); credit data monthly. Sellers: short sellers (17% of float) betting on credit. Buyers: growth funds if 2027 EPS guide beats.
sections.premortem: (1) Recession pushes charge-offs above 6%. (2) Another equity raise dilutes holders. (3) Regulatory changes hit loan-platform economics.
